title: Kaplansky decompositions of Polish modules
summary: Let $R$ be a countable ring. Given an $R$-module $A$, we call a decomposition $A = \bigoplus_{i \in I} N_i$ a Kaplansky decomposition if each $N_i$ is countable. We characterize the uncountable Polish $R$-modules that admit a Kaplansky decomposition: they are exactly the modules of the form $B \oplus M^ω$, where $B$ and $M$ are countable and $M$ is $Σ$-algebraically compact. The countable summand $B$ may moreover be taken to be an elementary submodule satisfying a closure condition, which makes $M^ω$ unique up to isomorphism, and hence an invariant of $A$.
